statement: Define an index i to have an ocean view when 0 <= i < len(heights) and for every j with i < j < len(heights), heights[j] < heights[i]. Under the preconditions, the function returns a result r (it does not fail), and r is exactly the list of all indices that have an ocean view, in increasing order. Equivalently: for every k with 0 <= k < len(r), r[k] has an ocean view; for every i that has an ocean view there is exactly one k with 0 <= k < len(r) and r[k] = i; and for every k with 0 <= k < len(r) - 1, r[k] < r[k + 1].
preconditions: len(heights) >= 1, len(heights) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(heights), 1 <= heights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Under the preconditions, find_buildings returns successfully: there exists a vector r such that the result is r. It does not fail with overflow, out-of-bounds, or panic.
